claim: KIIS reported in June 2021 that 73% of respondents identified as Orthodox, 9% as Greek Catholic and 7% as atheist; among Orthodox respondents, 58% identified with the Orthodox Church of Ukraine and 25% with the Ukrainian Orthodox Church of the Moscow Patriarchate.
limitations: Religious self-identification is not a direct measure of political loyalty, conflict propensity or institutional behavior; occupied territories are not fully represented.

claim: UNICEF reported in March-May 2021 that households along the contact line faced long-running disruptions to safe drinking water, with shelling repeatedly threatening critical water infrastructure and some villages dependent on delivered water.
limitations: Localized conflict-zone evidence; must not be generalized to nationwide household water access.

claim: UNICEF reported in August 2021 that infrastructure rehabilitation and new water towers had restored stable water supply to more than 21,000 people in conflict-affected eastern Ukraine, with additional villages planned.
limitations: Program reach is not evidence of region-wide normalization; it is a local counter-pressure.

claim: World Bank's September 2021 Systematic Country Diagnostic consultations stated that persistent institutional weaknesses impeded sustained growth, delivery of basic public services and job creation, while also identifying reform pathways and COVID recovery as adaptation channels.
limitations: Structural diagnosis does not establish an acute crisis or direct causal path to interstate war.
